backup.production_rule: Two migrations. The FIRST is a catch-up and a no-op against production: the meter-photo vision schema has been live since 2026-09-13 but was applied by hand and never recorded as a stay-site migration, so CI's baseline never had it and no pgTAP could touch it. Every statement in it is idempotent, and get_meter_photo_followups was verified byte-identical to the deployed function (md5(prosrc) 68844a6d99f94ab7c410f4d55806ee19, 1233 bytes, both sides, 2026-09-21). The SECOND adds one empty table, three functions, one partial index and two job_heartbeats rows. No existing column, row, function, policy or grant is changed by either. Nothing calls any of it until SPEC-11 session 2. Take a FRESH backup - the one used for meter_followup_resolution_20260921 is outside the one-hour window.

rollback.safe_until: always while SPEC-11 session 2 is unbuilt, because nothing calls any of this yet. Once the system-verifier function is deployed and scheduled, unschedule its two cron jobs first.

steps.name: do_not_roll_back_the_catchup
steps.action: The catch-up migration has nothing to undo: it only declared schema production already had. Rolling it back would drop live columns and a live function. Leave it.

steps.name: unschedule_the_cron_jobs_if_they_exist
steps.action: select cron.unschedule('system-verifier-hourly'); select cron.unschedule('system-verifier-daily'); - only needed once SPEC-11 session 2 has scheduled them

feature_flags.name: system_verifier_is_inert_until_session_2
feature_flags.required_state: This release adds no caller of its own. run_system_verifier_v1 reads and nothing else; apply_verifier_run_v1 and telegram_ack_verifier_finding_v1 are service_role only and nothing invokes them. The two auto-resolutions therefore cannot fire until the system-verifier Edge Function exists, is deployed and is scheduled, which is SPEC-11 session 2. Applying this release changes no observable behaviour anywhere.

compatibility.evidence: Two migrations, both additive. The catch-up only declares schema production has had since 2026-09-13; its two forward checks were run against production BEFORE shipping and both already return true, which is what a no-op must look like. The second adds one table, three functions, one index and two seed rows; nothing before this release names any of them. All eight checks (V1-V6, V11, V12) were run read-only against production on 2026-09-21 and returned clean. THREE real defects were caught before any of this went live, each by a different guard. (1) The production read-through: calendar_sync_log.status is 'ok', not the design's 'success', so V12 would have raised a red 'Airbnb feed has gone quiet' on a healthy feed the first time it ran. (2) CI's first run of the pgTAP: app_settings.value is JSONB, so a Concierge on auto reads as the quoted string "auto", never equals 'auto', and V11 would have raised a permanent yellow that nothing could clear. Fixed with #>> '{}', and pinned by a pair of assertions - fires on 'suggest', silent on 'auto' - because asserting only that a check fires would not have caught it. (3) The same CI run: meter_followup_resolution.sql died on 'column vision_electric does not exist', which is how the missing migration history was found at all. V1 was additionally proven positive against a synthetic overlapping pair through a VALUES CTE: one finding, keyed by both ids in sorted order, both guests named, red. pgTAP supabase/tests/database/system_verifier_phase1.sql, 32 assertions, every fixture created and rolled back inside the test transaction. It is the only cover for apply_verifier_run_v1's state machine (announce once, remind after 24h, resolve when gone, never resolve a check the scope did not run) and for both auto-resolutions, so a red database job on this release is the release failing, not a flaky test.
